summary: The plan is structurally valid and complete. All 50 spec-tree files have exactly one owner, ownership globs are disjoint across all 17 tasks, every spec task, component and AC maps to a task, DES-8/9/10 are placed correctly, and DES-2 holdout discipline is carried into t08/t11/t12/t16/t17. Two things must change before implementation. (1) t16 must run every documented command, including `npm test`, but it depends only on t13. Under maxConcurrency=2 the engine makes t16 ready while t15 is still claimed, so t16's suite run covers another subagent's half-finished contract tests. (2) The three plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate the foundation and integration phases are not in the submission. No task owns them, and `.eccode/**` is always allowed by task completion, so they are neither hash-pinned nor protected. The worst exposure is the dataset precheck, which is edited and run by the same task whose output it checks.

criteria.description: Plan passes `eccode plan validate` (schema, known phases/owners/deps, no later-phase deps, no cycles, no ownership warnings)
Tasks cover the spec: every file in the spec directory tree, every spec workflow task 1-16 (merge 10+11 and split of 14 justified), and every AC/test file in the Testing Strategy table maps to a task
Every task has owner, dependencies, inputs, outputs, file ownership, acceptance criteria and a verification method/command
File ownership: globs pairwise disjoint across all tasks (not only concurrent ones), each spec-tree file has exactly one owner, and each task's verification command runs only test files it owns
Dependency correctness: no task is blocked by a missing dependency, and no task's required checks run files owned by a task that can still be in progress concurrently

DES-2 holdout discipline: rules author reads dataset.json only, measures only with eval:tune, never runs the precheck or full mode; freeze precedes rules files by phase order; hygiene test is the only npm-test reader of holdout.json; first full-mode run is t17 by delivery-lead and is counted
Design review findings placed: DES-8 in t04 AC + core-modules phase criterion (design-vectors.js left untouched, justified), DES-9 in t08 AC + pipeline criterion, DES-10 as t06 in t11 dependencies

Phases independently verifiable with pinned, reviewed instruments: each phase criterion names a command, and the commands the plan relies on are part of the reviewed submission and cannot be changed silently by the tasks they verify
Buildable by parallel subagents under maxConcurrency=2: waves are feasible, longest tasks are scheduled first, same-phase concurrent tasks share no files

findings.title: t16-readme runs `npm test` but does not depend on t14/t15, so it can run against another subagent's half-finished contract tests
findings.detail: t16's third acceptance criterion requires every documented command except full-mode eval to be run once from the project root and to work. The documented commands include `npm test`, whose glob `test/**/*.test.js` covers t14's and t15's files. t16 depends only on t13-app-wiring. I simulated the integration phase with the engine's own readyTasks() and the plan's dependencies at maxConcurrency=2 (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). All of t14, t15 and t16 are ready at once. After t14 completes while t15 is still claimed, t16 is the next ready task. Its `npm test` run then either fails on t15's in-progress files, so t16 fails or burns retries for reasons outside its ownership, or it passes on an incomplete suite, so the README's claim that `npm test` works is not established. This contradicts plan.md's own claim that a subagent is never failed by another subagent's half-finished files.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when either (a) t16.dependencies includes t14-contract-http and t15-contract-modes-privacy, with the plan.md wave table updated to show t14 ∥ t15, then t16, then t17; or (b) t16's acceptance criterion excludes `npm test` from the commands t16 runs (t17 already runs the full suite) and says so explicitly. `eccode plan validate` must still pass.

findings.title: The plan check scripts that verify t01, t02 and t16 and gate two phases are not in the submission, have no owner, and are editable by any task
findings.detail: The verification.command values of t01-scaffold, t02-eval-dataset and t16-readme, and the criteria of the foundation and integration phases, call .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/{scaffold-check,dataset-precheck,readme-check}.js. The plan submission hashes only plan.json and plan.md. No task's file globs cover these scripts, and lib/tasks.js ALWAYS_ALLOWED (`.eccode/**`) lets any task change them without an ownership error at completion (ev:ev-muynyxxl-01ff66ef). So the instruments are neither reviewed nor pinned by this gate. The worst case is dataset-precheck.js, the pre-freeze guard for the frozen evaluation data (E5/D6). The test-engineer in t02 runs it against their own dataset and could change it without the engine or a later reviewer noticing. I read all three scripts, and on inspection they implement what plan.md describes. scaffold-check accepts the spec's exact §Deployment package.json and .env.example and rejects a mutated package.json (ev:ev-muynynlv-01f7a511). The problem is pinning, not content.
findings.recommendation: Resolved when the resubmission includes the three check scripts as submission artifacts, so their sha256 values are recorded with the plan. plan.md must also state that no implementation task may modify .eccode/artifacts/plan/checks/**. The foundation and integration phase criteria (or the phase submission routine) must require the phase reviewer to confirm the scripts' sha256 values still equal the plan submission before relying on their output.

findings.title: t17's chained verification command conflicts with its own 'complete even if the full eval fails' criterion
findings.detail: t17.verification.command is `npm test && npm run eval && node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`. If the first full-mode eval exits 1 because a holdout floor is missed, the chain stops and design-vectors never runs. Re-running the same command would be a second full-mode run, which E5 forbids inside the task. The acceptance criteria already say the task completes on the passing npm test evidence, so the intent is right, but the literal command steers an implementer the wrong way.
findings.recommendation: Express t17's verification as three separate `eccode evidence run` steps, `npm test`, `npm run eval` (exactly once) and `node .eccode/artifacts/design/design-vectors.js`, instead of one && chain.

findings.title: Some cross-task needs are satisfied only by phase ordering, not by declared dependencies
findings.detail: t14's http.test.js (static responses, AC11 headers, traversal 404) and spawned servers in t13/t15 need public/ from t07. Neither t14 nor t13 depends on t07, directly or transitively. This is safe because phase gates run strictly in sequence and core-modules is approved before rules-and-wiring and integration. t13's use of the t03 helpers is covered transitively through t06. Also, the core-modules phase criterion for DES-8 lists two of the three reject vectors that t04's criterion lists (the Arabic-Indic digit vector is missing).
findings.recommendation: Optional: add t07-ui to t14-contract-http.dependencies for explicitness, and list all three DES-8 reject vectors in the core-modules phase criterion.
